summary: The three-loop cycle is complete. The next priority is to account for the complete original homogeneous remainder and establish the changed-diagonal hypotheses before attempting a second correction. The alternatives remain observable identification and complete graph scaling. These are plans, not additional executed loops.

next_goals.title: Account for the complete remainder before a second correction
next_goals.target: Enumerate and bound the actual additional remainder E from the original transformed homogeneous Hamiltonian, including its scalar, reference-diagonal and mixing pieces. Derive the next reference operator's domain, local spectral conditions and remaining support-weight budget. Freeze a second-step claim only after those premises are available; the selected-source contraction cannot be iterated unchanged.

next_goals.title: Test a cancellation-aware readout with complete errors
next_goals.target: Audit the exact combination m3(B5)-q m3(B4)=2q^13(1-q^2) as a possible ratio refinement. Derive numerator cancellation without assuming that state, averaging or measurement errors cancel. Retain a denominator bound, fixed physical observation convention and nuisance parameters; any continuous inverse or calibrated clock needs its own proof.

next_goals.title: Increase the physical graph with complete channel control
next_goals.target: Freeze the next Gauss-invariant SU(2) graph and retained space; enumerate its Gram null relations, all reached and omitted channels, and the true centering and denominator errors. Compare graph-dependent constants only after that completeness check. A larger matrix or favorable graph-size trend does not supply a volume or continuum theorem.
